flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me a little about yourself and why early childhood education matters to you.
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q1 Attempt 1]
Well, growing up, I wasn't really that good in school. I'm also an IEP kid. And as I got older, the teachers, when I came out here to Palmdale, had really helped me that I extended my education, doing really well, so good that they let me do independent studies. And I was doing that in some college. And I was stuck between being a nurse or wanting to go into early education. And then I got a job with my mom at Golden Poppy for about four to five years. And then I was volunteering with the kindergarten group. And one of the TA teachers that was friends and coworkers, and she was like, why not just do it yourself? You're here, you're helping the kids. So I decided to quit my job, take some time off, and decided to go back to school and also want to open up a daycare. So that's a little postponed right now. And I've always been around special needs kids because my dad also was doing that for 25 years, and he's on a business truck. So I'm used to different personalities, people being different. And I just really wanted to go into that field. And also, my brother has ADHD and all that, too. So I'm kind of used to being around different kids and levels, how to deal with them, the patients and stuff. I was on noon duty, supervising the kids, cleaning up after them, watching. I'm on the playground. And then on my spare time, I would come in to help the kids who needed help with homework and the parents who was kind of older or didn't speak Spanish. So I would help them with their work. So they want to get.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child was having a really hard moment emotionally. What did you notice about what they were feeling, and how did you respond?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q3 Attempt 1]
Um, it was like a surname. It was a little girl. Usually she's like really, really happy. And I kind of noticed her from the back when I was helping with another student. And it turns out that she was losing her grandmother. And she was very scared of getting close to other people in the family members thinking that they was going to, she started to realize what the word death means. So I had to kind of not go too in detail because, you know, teachers are not supposed to do that far, but just give her a little assurance and stuff. And her parents actually had came in and thanked me for that, just giving a listening ear.

But yeah, I wasn't like yelling, but I took it and just talk it through with there. Oh, he was pushing another kid on top of the slide. So, and then he didn't see me on the walk around.
